steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: There's this one proverb Blaze always pulls out. How did it go again––?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: The shortest distance between two points is a straight line.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: That's the one.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: I have a conjecture. You rainforest folk have the terrible misfortune of living in that dump, so you've been compensated with extremely good luck in other areas.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: What other explanation is there for why the lot of you haven't gone extinct yet? It doesn't make any sense.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: It proves our way of life is good for keeping us alive.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: High Priest, what are Durin cities like?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Uhh, I don't remember. A little too boring to talk about.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: I spent some time in the underground world a century or so ago and the only thing I can remember is that it was a nasty place chock-full of imbeciles.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Less interesting than watching Originium slugs sleep by the river.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Though, heh, you young kids ought to experience things on your own. You need to have the kind of drive and ambition that I did!

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: By the way, turn left at the next junction, and DON'T jump down!

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: How much longer now, High Priest?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Good question. There's no end to the road called life. No matter how far you've come, you can only keep moving forward— plus, there's a geezer like me watching over you.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Oh, if you meant how far we are from the city, if you could drop right through the rocks like I can, you need to go down another five or six hundred meters.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Zumama, how the hell did you put up with this guy up so long? He won't shut up.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: He's usually not as noisy around the machines.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Does this chainsaw blade count as a machine?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Harrumph! No manners!

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Would you look at that. Worked like a charm.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: This is it... We're here!

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Uhh, the 'Great Aquapit?'

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Let's set aside the Durins' naming sense for now.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: This waterpark already looked pretty insane from the distance, but it's even more incredible up-close!

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Is this how Durins live all the time?!

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Cowabunga!!

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: When did he change into a swimsuit?

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: E-Elysium, please be careful!

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Woah, that was a close one! Are you alright? Didn't spill your drink, did you?

steps.name: Durin Youth
steps.text: Well... that's weird. How'd you surface-dwellers end up down here? Never seen you people around before.

steps.name: Durin Youth
steps.text: And this guy looks about as stupid as a Durin.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Hello, sir. We were invited here by Stitch Canvas.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: He said, uh, he wanted us to help him with a little favor!

steps.name: Durin Youth
steps.text: Stitch Canvas, huh... Would you look at that, he actually came back.

steps.name: Durin Youth
steps.text: I thought he was going to say goodbye to this city for good, just like that respectable teacher of his.

steps.name: Durin Youth
steps.text: As much as I'd like to offer you our famous Durin hospitality, welcoming folk that we are, I sadly can't while Stitch is running around causing havoc and ignoring all our ways.

steps.name: Durin Youth
steps.text: Let me introduce myself first. I am Catch Lightrace, this city's design representative.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: No need to be nervous. It'll be over in no time.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: What... is the meaning of this?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Hmm? Did the atmosphere just get a little weird all of a sudden? I can't handle all these people trying to toast me at the same time.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Are you guys...?

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Trying to pick a fight?! I'm not afraid of you shorties!

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: You're gonna get a taste of the combat skills Gavial taught me! Phew... Take a sturdy stance, and put your hips into it!

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Come at me!

steps.name: Flustered Durin
steps.text: Wh-What is she doing?! Is she gonna clobber us with her stick?

steps.name: Nervous Durin
steps.text: Gyaaaah! Stay away from me!

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Hey, hey! What are you people doing?! Stop! Stop, I tell you!!

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Huh? I thought we were going to fight?

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Why would Durins do such a pointless thing?!

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Put your weapons away and come with me!

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Ahem! Citizens of Zeruertza, this is this quarter's four hundred and seventeenth referendum.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Following our previous vote on this month's general background music, we decided on the color of our street lights for the week during the last referendum. Now, we must answer a new question.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Since this question isn't particularly important, the individuals here today are enough of a quorum to represent Zeruertza.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Today's question is: Zeruertza has just welcomed new guests. Should we accept them or not?

steps.name: Topsy-Turvy Durin
steps.text: What guests?

steps.name: Topsy-Turvy Durin
steps.text: I heard something about a guy who doesn't drink?

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Ah, no, it's these ones standing right in front of us.

steps.name: Topsy-Turvy Durin
steps.text: Cheers, brother! Isn't it crazy that there's a Durin out there who doesn't drink?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Yeah, that's totally crazy. Cheers!

steps.name: Topsy-Turvy Durin
steps.text: Let's finish chugging this barrel, then we can go play in the water.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Hah, make sure to keep those eyelids peeled! You have to see what us surface-dwellers can do!

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Tomimi, sorry if I sound like a broken record, but are you sure everything's alright at Rhodes Island?

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Uh, p-probably?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: You're always welcome to come back if things aren't working out. Be careful— don't underestimate the amount of damage a bad environment can do to you!

steps.name: Topsy-Turvy Durin
steps.text: Hurry it up, Catch! We've got a lot of stuff to take care of!

steps.name: Topsy-Turvy Durin
steps.text: Brother, have you ever heard of a sport called surfing?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Surfing, you say? That might as well be my middle name!
Objection!
This guy can't be trusted!

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Ah, yeah. I knew things weren't going to be that simple...

steps.name: Absent-Minded Durin
steps.text: Hey you, drunk Liberi over there!

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Inam, they must be talking to you, because I certainly amn't drunk. Not a bit.

steps.name: Absent-Minded Durin
steps.text: I AM talking to you, guy with the stein!

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Alright. Whaddya want?

steps.name: Wobbly Durin
steps.text: You'd better come out and pick a side: noble mead, or lame-ass whiskey!

steps.name: Absent-Minded Durin
steps.text: We of the Old Karl Mead fan club graciously welcomed you into our fold, and now you're hanging out with those hoity-toity whiskey-sippers? My disappointment is immeasurable!

steps.name: Wobbly Durin
steps.text: Not too long ago, we had our arms over each other's shoulders, shouting 'Long Live Mead' together. But I turn around for a second and you go off to play with those uppity kids?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Err, um, I think they're both great...

steps.name: Absent-Minded Durin
steps.text: Oh no you don't! We don't take kindly to fence-sitters around here!

steps.name: Topsy-Turvy Durin
steps.text: Haha, you're a joke. You can't know what's good and what's bad without a point of reference. Isn't that right, brother?

steps.name: Topsy-Turvy Durin
steps.text: There's nothing to be afraid of. Speak your mind, and let the words of praise flow for our great whiskey. That is, if you want to stay in Zeruertza––

steps.name: Wobbly Durin
steps.text: Hey, stop threatening him, you despicable whiskey-sipper!

steps.name: Topsy-Turvy Durin
steps.text: Gah. Your mead's baby stuff! Might as well drink it out of a bottle!

steps.name: Absent-Minded Durin
steps.text: Let's throw down in front of the Big Cask tonight then! Walk the walk if you talk the talk!

steps.name: Topsy-Turvy Durin
steps.text: Hah, you wanna see who can chug more of your baby brew? You have my attention!

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Wait, stop right there! The referenda we hold here in the forum are sacred! Talk about drinking somewhere else––

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Raise your hand, and let your vote be known. The minority obeys the will of the majority— that is the eternal lodestar of Zeruertza.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Begin the counting of the votes!

steps.name: Wobbly Durin
steps.text: If you're raising your hand, then I'm not!

steps.name: Topsy-Turvy Durin
steps.text: I'm raising my hand whether you like it or not! Piss off!

steps.name: Wobbly Durin
steps.text: Just wait 'til we get to the water slide. I'm gonna splash your brains out!

steps.name: Topsy-Turvy Durin
steps.text: With what, that ridiculous 'technique' of yours?

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Alright, not bad. A solemnly conducted vote.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: In what world does this count as solemn?

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: The votes have been counted, and the results are clear.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: The people of Zeruertza have made their decision: play to your hearts' content, surface-dwellers.

steps.name: Durin Attendees
steps.text: Cheers!!

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: By the way, I welcome you as an architect. That gorgeous edifice sitting atop the lake is my pride and joy. You are welcome to play your hearts out beneath it.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: You're talking about that 'Great Aquapit' over there?

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: I didn't come up with the name. It was something we all voted on!

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Did they tack more stuff onto the 'Great Aquapit?' It looks even more hideous than the last time I saw it.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: That's Catch's masterpiece, you know? You really shouldn't badmouth it in front of him.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: He's not worthy of my constructive criticism anyway. Or rather, there's no way to fix it in the first place!

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: That malformed, twisted structure... Just looking at it makes me want to pass out! How can the people of Zeruertza continue to suffer him as the design representative?

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Probably because folks really love playing on the big slide.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: If I were calling the shots...

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: You'd use béton brute to construct... uh, an array of squares.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: You still don't know me well enough, Edge. I'd just put a long, narrow strip of concrete there. Minimalism is beauty.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Huh? What about the slide then?

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: I suppose there wouldn't be any harm in slanting it a little...

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Ahem, back to the issue at hand.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: There don't seem to be any major issues with the dome right now, but I'm still worried.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Since the earthquake over six months ago, the leak that sprung in the dome has been getting worse and worse. Is that your idea of no major issues?

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: I'm just telling you what the people of Zeruertza think. The water flow increased? Makes for a more stimulating experience. The temperature control stopped working? Even better, that just means the summer's not over yet!

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: As for the Originium detection system... Well, no active Originium layers have been detected near Zeruertza for over two decades!

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Hmph. A short-sighted bunch.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: So, you...

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: I'm not fixing it. What's worth saving about this cheap, rickety dome? I've said it a million times.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Were you not looking for a solution when you first went up to the surface? Were you not thinking about ways to restore the dome?

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Absolutely not. I was just trying to hide from you because you won't shut up.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Now that's a little harsh, isn't it? Just a few months ago, I was voted into the Top 100 List of Zeruertza's Nicest Elders.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Alright, enough of that. I know you're concerned about the state of the dome.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: But if Catch can't even solve the issue with the dome's integrity, then forget occupying the design representative's seat, he should get the hell out of Zeruertza.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: If we're just talking outcomes, there shouldn't be any safety concerns regarding the dome at this point.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: We can leave the temperature control system alone, since our beloved citizens are having a good time anyway. After they get tired of it, maybe they'll raise their hands and decide to turn Zeruertza into a walk-in freezer.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: As for that Originium detection system, if you ask me, it was never that reliable to begin with. But since you've been chasing me around everywhere, I assume that's what you're most worried about? I do have a plan for that actually.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: It'd be better for us to rebuild the railway bridge that was damaged by the earthquake, re-excavate the collapsed tunnels, and directly install the Originium detection instruments there for more accurate readings.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: From the very beginning, the dome was over-engineered to try to do too many things at once.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: You'd rather take a massive detour like that than directly work on the dome? Look, even if Finch up and left without saying anything, that's still your work together, master and pupil...

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: We're done here, okay?

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Stop before I actually get mad, Edge.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: ...Fine.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Right now, the problem of Originium detection takes top priority.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: I picked up a few people up on the surface who will probably come in handy. Their hodgepodge of skills is likely enough to repair Zeruertza's railway.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Now, we only need to...

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Pardon the interruption, but are those handy people from the surface you're talking about...

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Is that one flying through the sky right now?

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Waheyyyyy!

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: When you, Zumama, and Kemar first joined Rhodes Island, I didn't think much of it. But now that I've seen this guy...

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Be honest with me, Tomimi. Is it really that easy to swindle a paycheck out of your company?

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Elysium is actually a skilled guide and a communications specialist...

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Well, anyway! Maybe this is who he really is!

steps.name: Durin Hawker
steps.text: Here's the sweet fruit wine you wanted~

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Thank you!

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Uhh, how should I pay? Or rather, how'd you buy all that other stuff before?

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: I told the nice tailor granny a few stories about Gavial, and she was so happy she gave me these clothes for free!

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: As for me... The drinks were covered by my good friends from the fan club, and I put the food on Stitch's tab.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: I guess you'll probably survive, no matter where you get tossed.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: That's one of the qualities of a professional guide!

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Ma'am, go ahead and put our drinks on Mr. Stitch's tab as well. He won't mind.

steps.name: Durin Hawker
steps.text: You got it!

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Haha, that guy's stingier than you'd think. Here, let me pay for those drinks.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: I am quite proud of this amusement park after all. Naturally, I hope you'll have a great time.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Mr. Lightrace, do you and Mr. Canvas know each other well?

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Depends what you mean by 'well.'

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: When we were young, we ran into each other a lot, since we were competing. We've gone head-to-head over several projects, some of which I won, some of which he won.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: The only project neither one of us could secure was this dome above our heads.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: We both have ideas for how we'd like to improve Zeruertza's iconic dome, and for a few years, we practically met every day––

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: During the referendum meetings, we both worked hard to prove that our respective ideas for the dome renovation were better.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: But in the end, neither of us managed to win over a majority of Zeruertza's population.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: After all, the dome is the legacy of Master Finch, the design representative who came before me.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: And Stitch, as his student, is also...

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Forget it. There are some things I'm not meant to say. You'd be better off asking him yourself.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Catch, my dear bro, why is someone as young as you talking like a withered old man? 'When we were young?' Come on.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Just follow Elysium's lead. Keep your heart pure, and face life with a smile! Instead of lamenting days bygone, come enjoy a drink with us––

steps.name: Durin Hawker
steps.text: Liberi man, your extra-large barrel of ice-cold beat-the-heat ale is here!

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Help yourselves, everyone! Our good friend Catch wants us to have a good time, so how could we possibly disappoint his expectations?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: So, my good brother, mind if I order some more? The folks from the fan club aren't paying for other drinks, and there's still so much I want to try.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Are you sure you're not a Durin on stilts?

steps.name: Contemplative Lupo
steps.text: Are there any other ads I have to write..?

steps.name: Contemplative Lupo
steps.text: Oh, right.

steps.name: Contemplative Lupo
steps.text: 'How should I describe the feeling of this long-leaf dew rolling down my throat? How ought I praise it without using words so pedestrian?'

steps.name: Contemplative Lupo
steps.text: 'Tis as if I could swallow a cloud, or pluck a string of spring rain's pearls.'

steps.name: Contemplative Lupo
steps.text: 'Tis as if I could feel the falling of winter's last two snowflakes...'

steps.name: Contemplative Lupo
steps.text: Uhh, they probably have no idea what falling snowflakes are, so maybe I'll go with a more Durin metaphor.

steps.name: Contemplative Lupo
steps.text: 'Two super-frosty fruit-flavored ice cubes fall into a marvelous explosion of flavor––'

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Ugh, that hurts––

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: The High Priest was right, we really shouldn't have jumped down.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: It's been a real long time since I've felt like my bones were gonna fall apart. Probably the last time we fought.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Yeah. Now I think I'm starting to hallucinate. About fruit-flavored ice cubes and rum. Think it might be an aftereffect of our fall?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Huh? Why's there a Lupo sleeping here?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Do you think... this might be our fault?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Probably not... right? Uhh, think I should treat her?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Did you bring your medical kit?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Dr. Kal'tsit once said that a true master of medicine can resolve most problems with her bare hands.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Did she now?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Well, I don't remember her exact words, but that's the gist I took from it. Alright, where to start...?

steps.name: Lupo
steps.text: *gasp*!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Oh, she's awake. I haven't even gotten started yet.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Um... Are you alright?

steps.name: Lupo
steps.text: Ugh, my head's still spinning...

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Sorry, I think the two of us might've bumped into you earlier. Need me to inspect you?

steps.name: Lupo
steps.text: What are you doing here?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Come again...?

steps.name: Lupo
steps.text: How did you two find this place?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Mind if we ask for directions? Do you know if there's a magical underground city here, or something like that?

steps.name: Lupo
steps.text: You came from the surface.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Weird thing to say. You didn't?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: We heard something terrible was about to happen underground, so...

steps.name: Lupo
steps.text: You've finally come, surface-dwellers.

steps.name: Lupo
steps.text: 'Naturally, those who come with chainsaw and axe in hand can only spell calamity for this pure garden.'

steps.name: Lupo
steps.text: ...... 'The beast of civilization finally sheds all pretense of hiding its razor-sharp fangs, baring its gigantic maw before us...'

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I see, that makes sense. A wild beast with a huge mouth and razor-sharp teeth. Don't worry, I'll handle this.

steps.name: Lupo
steps.text: Huh? No, that was a rhetorical flourish...

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: As long as the thing's less than ten meters wide, I'm confident I can take it down clean. Perfect timing too, since I've been itching to get a good workout!

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Mind showing us the way, Miss Lupo? Is it over here?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Maybe it'll be faster if we keep jumping down.

steps.name: Lupo
steps.text: Stop, surface-dwellers! The blood on you will...

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Don't worry. I know how to control my strength so it's not going to splatter all over the place.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Zumama, ready for round two?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Right behind you.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Hold on tight, Miss Lupo.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: You can trust Gavial. She's an expert when it comes to fighting.

steps.name: Lupo
steps.text: Uh, actually, there's another way... Hey? Hey!!
